about: Errors arc (and the tools it calls) really print, each with where the words come from, what it means and the fix. diagnose.py matches `pattern` (a Python regex) against a command's stdout+stderr. A fix that touches a global file (~/.tars, ~/.arc, ~/.claude) or anything remote is asked first.

issues.source: git's own message, surfaced by arc (crates/apps/cli/src/cli/dispatch.rs require_git_repo)
issues.cause: arc ran outside a git work tree.
issues.fix: cd into the project, or `git init` it if the person agrees.

issues.pattern: (command not found: arc|arc: command not found|No such file or directory: 'arc')
issues.cause: arc is not installed, or its directory is not on PATH.
issues.fix: stage `binary`: install from getarc, or add the directory holding arc to PATH.

issues.source: clap, when the installed arc predates the verb
issues.cause: the installed arc is older than this route: the verb was added later (getarc's newest release may predate it).
issues.fix: compare `arc --version` with the release page; if getarc has nothing newer, stop and say so — do not fake the verb with another.

issues.source: scripts/fetch_arc.py (GitHub's download URL for a --version or asset that does not exist)
issues.cause: the --version tag is not published on getarc (yet), or the release (or the --from mirror) has no asset for this platform.
issues.fix: check the tag or mirror with the person and the release page; do not fall back to another release without saying so.

issues.pattern: no providers found in your tars registry
issues.cause: the tars config has no [providers.<id>] (or arc read a different tars home than you think).
issues.fix: stage `tars`: define one provider in <tars home>/config.toml (ask before writing that global file); pass the same --tars_home to every arc call.

issues.cause: the tars config file could not be read or parsed; the rest of the line is tars's own reason (an unknown key in a provider table is refused: tars-config providers.rs deny_unknown_fields).
issues.fix: show the person the rest of the line; fix the named key in the tars config with their consent.

issues.pattern: missing credential: env var `([A-Za-z0-9_]+)` is not set
issues.cause: the provider reads its key from an environment variable that is not set in the shell arc runs in.
issues.fix: the person exports it themselves (shell profile or `source .env`). Never ask for the key's value, never write it to .arc/.

issues.pattern: arc init needs an interactive terminal
issues.cause: expected when an agent runs `arc init`: stdin is not a terminal, so arc left .arc/config.toml.example instead of asking.
issues.fix: ask the person for the critic and fixer provider ids, copy the example to .arc/config.toml and fill [roles] with them (the example's own instruction).

issues.cause: .arc/config.toml is already there; arc init does not overwrite it.
issues.fix: probe the stage: if [roles] already resolve, the stage is done. Overwrite only if the person asks.

issues.cause: an old-shape .arc/config.toml still defines providers; arc reads providers only from tars.
issues.fix: move each [providers.<id>] to the tars config (ask first — global file), then delete the section from .arc/config.toml.

issues.cause: [roles] has neither that role nor `default`.
issues.fix: add `<role> = "<tars provider id>"` (or `default`) under [roles].

issues.cause: the fixer never falls back to `default`.
issues.fix: add `fixer = "<tars provider id>"`, a different model family from the critic.

issues.cause: a [roles] value names an id the tars config does not define (often: arc read another tars home).
issues.fix: use one of the listed ids, or define that provider in tars; pass the same --tars_home everywhere.

issues.pattern: fixer pipeline: failed to build provider '([^']+)'
issues.cause: the fixer's id is not in the tars config, or that entry does not parse; the rest of the line is tars's words.
issues.fix: fix the tars entry the line names.

issues.cause: a step holds `${{ … }}`; arc runs no expressions, and a merge gate with one refuses every PR.
issues.fix: rewrite with shell variables (`$NODE_ENV`, an `env:` value) and re-run `arc workflow … --list`.

issues.cause: a `uses:` arc does not read (only checkout, setup-node/python/go and dtolnay/rust-toolchain are read, as machine checks).
issues.fix: replace it with plain `run:` steps; the tool it installed must already be on the merge machine.

issues.pattern: no job named (\S+); the file defines:
issues.cause: --job names a job the file does not have.
issues.fix: use one of the jobs the line lists.

issues.cause: arc names the repo from `origin`; this clone has none.
issues.fix: the person adds the GitHub remote (creating a remote repo is an outward action — ask).

issues.cause: a pipeline lookup found no tenant for this repo in this machine's ~/.arc/machine.toml: no review service serves it here. `arc local-review` and `arc fix` never ask (they use the clone's own .arc/review.db); this comes from arc's services.
issues.fix: on the pipeline machine, register the repo with `arc-server install <clone>` (or `arc-server tenant add <clone>`); see docs/user-guide/onboarding.md.

issues.pattern: post-commit-gate (\S+): could not decide, so no review — (.*)
issues.source: crates/apps/cli/src/cli/local_review_dispatch.rs:148 (the post-commit hook prints it to the terminal and .arc/critic.log since #3412); docs/user-guide/coding-agents.md
issues.cause: the post-commit hook asked whether to review this commit and could not decide, so it reviewed nothing. The reason follows the dash — most often the branch has no local PR yet (`this checkout's branch holds no open local PR — run `arc local-review` first`).
issues.fix: read the reason after the dash and follow its own row (no_pr_on_record, or whichever row matches it). The commit itself succeeded; nothing to undo.

issues.pattern: this checkout's branch holds no open local PR — run `arc local-review` first
issues.cause: arc fix works on the branch's local PR in this clone's .arc/review.db, and this branch has none open.
issues.fix: `arc local-review` opens it in this clone; nothing leaves the machine.

issues.pattern: cannot tell who is submitting — not in an agent session and no `gh` login
issues.cause: `arc local-review`, `arc fix` and `arc submit` name who ran them: the agent session they run in (Claude Code, Codex, agy), else the `gh` login. This shell has neither.
issues.fix: run it from the person's coding agent, or have the person run `gh auth login` (their account — ask).

issues.cause: ~/.arc/client.toml names no board, so the client does not know where the pipeline is.
issues.fix: on the pipeline machine `arc-server tenant url web` prints the address; write `web = "http://<host>:<port>"` to ~/.arc/client.toml (ask first — global file).

issues.pattern: HEAD is not on a feature branch
issues.cause: `arc submit` ran on a detached HEAD or the default branch; a PR belongs to a feature branch.
issues.fix: check out a feature branch (`git switch -c <name>`, after asking) and run arc submit again.

issues.cause: origin/HEAD is not set in this clone, so arc cannot tell which branch the change lands on (probe.py's *_on_target criteria say the same).
issues.fix: `git remote set-head origin --auto` (it reads origin; ask first), then run again.

issues.cause: presubmit.toml does not read: a misspelt key, no [[checks]], no or a zero timeout_seconds, or one over 86400.
issues.fix: fix the key the line names (docs/user-guide/configuration.md, <repo>/presubmit.toml) and run `arc presubmit` again.

issues.cause: a check's command spells {base} / {target} / {affected} and the run was not given the flag that fills it; no check ran.
issues.fix: `git fetch origin`, then pass `--target origin/<target> --base "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/<target>)"`.

issues.pattern: the working tree has uncommitted changes, and a check passes only on HEAD's own tree
issues.cause: a check's pass counts for HEAD, so it runs only on a clean tree (untracked files included).
issues.fix: commit or remove the paths the line lists (ask before discarding anything), then run again.

issues.pattern: is too old — refusing to start \(need git >= (\d+\.\d+)\)
issues.cause: the merge server merges with `git merge-tree --write-tree`, which arrived in git 2.38.
issues.fix: the person installs a newer git on the pipeline machine (a system package — ask), then restarts the service.

issues.pattern: refusing to start: arc takes no input from the environment
issues.cause: a service found ARC_* variables outside its allow-list; the lines after it name each one and what replaced it.
issues.fix: remove each named variable (the unit, the shell profile, `systemctl --user show-environment`); put the setting in ~/.arc/machine.toml as the line says.

issues.pattern: does not exist — a service reads its configuration from it
issues.cause: ~/.arc/machine.toml is not there yet.
issues.fix: stage `machine`: write [machine] (ask first — global file); `arc-server install <clone>` adds the [[tenant]].

issues.pattern: \[machine\] expose = true, but no address is written
issues.cause: expose = true needs the IP address the board and the chat server listen on.
issues.fix: add `address = "<this machine's IP>"` under [machine].

issues.pattern: `([^`]+)` is no setting of a tenant
issues.cause: `arc-server tenant set` was given a key a [[tenant]] does not have.
issues.fix: `arc-server tenant show <owner/name>` lists the keys; review routes are edited in machine.toml, not with tenant set.

issues.cause: `arc-server tenant check|show|set <owner/name>` named a repo machine.toml does not register.
issues.fix: register the clone with `arc-server install <clone>`, or use a name `arc-server tenant list` prints.

issues.pattern: (\S+) is not a tenant of this environment \(tenants:
issues.cause: a per-repo service (arc-server@ / arc-review@) started for a name machine.toml does not register; the unit instance is the tenant name with `/` turned into `-`.
issues.fix: enable the unit for a registered tenant (`arc-server tenant list`), or register the clone first.

issues.pattern: refusing to start — `arc-server tenant check (\S+)` fails:
issues.cause: arc-server or arc-review ran the tenant's offline checks at start and one said FAIL; the lines under it name which.
issues.fix: run `arc-server tenant check <owner/name>` and fix each FAIL line (most often: the clone has uncommitted paths, or is not at its real path); then start the service again.

issues.cause: ~/.arc/client.toml has a key other than `web`, or is not TOML.
issues.fix: leave exactly one line, `web = "http://<address>:<port>"` (what `arc-server tenant url web` prints on the pipeline machine).

issues.source: systemctl (systemd's own words), when the shell has no user manager session
issues.cause: `systemctl --user` could not reach this user's systemd manager — usually a shell started with su/sudo, or no lingering for the user.
issues.fix: log in as the service user directly (ssh), and turn lingering on: `loginctl enable-linger $USER` (ask first).
